content.a4a95443e2ca: "AI Steering." Uses a neural network to steer instead of traditional math formulas. Note: In sunnypilot 2026.002+, NNLC and Enforce Torque Control are mutually exclusive. Issue #2019 reports low-speed oscillation with NNLC on a Prius Prime using Chestnut models. Start with torque control and NNLC off for the updated modern-vehicle presets; this report does not establish a universal fault across all cars.
content.e91537697799: "Adaptive Torque Steering." Replaces older steering methods with a high-accuracy torque model. If your car wanders or feels sloppy in curves, turning on Self-Tune lets sunnypilot automatically dial in the steering friction and strength for your specific car.
content.a628bda54bfb: "Always-On Steering." The car steers for you even if you are in full control of the speed. You can coast, brake, or accelerate without the steering turning off. Brake hold is a separate condition: open PRs #2031 and #2039 propose pause/engagement protection. Ordinary brake-pedal behavior does not guarantee steering remains active during brake hold.
content.80337da25ab3: "Auto-Speed Limit." Automatically aligns your cruise control to the legal speed limit (plus your custom offset, e.g., +5 mph).
content.4d1661e370a7: "Brain Swapper." Choose between different AI models trained on various driving styles (smooth highway, sharp curves, aggressive city). Tune steer delay and turn desire speed to suit your preferences. Refresh Models was added to comma four in master by PR #2018; use it while parked when no download/refresh is running. Clear Cache removes downloaded model cache. Selector version 20 whole-file manifests remain an open proposal (#2015).
content.2d1b10b470d6: "Button Step Sizer." Customize your steering wheel buttons so one tap changes speed by 1 mph and holding it jumps by 5 mph (or any step size you choose).
content.ae6f3995825f: "City/Highway Switcher." Automatically switches modes based on context. Smooth highway cruising in Chill Mode, and intelligent slowing for intersections and stop signs when needed.
content.5c767ba4413e: "Cloud Companion." Connects your device to sunnylink.ai so you can backup your settings, tune parameters from your phone, and link your GitHub account for sponsor features.
content.aafd8791ce7a: "Cruise Hacker." If your car doesn't support full self-driving gas/brake, this feature simulates your steering wheel buttons to force the car to slow down for curves or speed limits. SCC-L is a proposed extension in issue #1846 to use model longitudinal output as an ICBM speed-target source. It is not an available SCC-V/SCC-M option.
content.7404f2b3474e: "Custom Gas & Brake." Replaces your car's factory radar cruise control with sunnypilot's own throttle and braking logic, allowing for smoother slowdowns and custom car following distances.
content.77177f9ef010: "Eyes-On Curve Slowdown." The car sees a sharp turn coming and smoothly slows down before entering the curve, just like a human driver would.
content.4fedff16852a: "Hands-Free Lane Change." You flick the turn signal, sunnypilot verifies the blind spot is clear, waits your preferred delay timer, and executes a smooth lane change automatically.
content.000ee1a23f4d: "Hyundai Gas Pedal Fix." If your Kia/Hyundai accelerates too slowly or feels sluggish when resuming from stops, switching this to "Dynamic" improves throttle response.
content.06668bf2593c: "Map-Based Curve Slowdown." The car looks at the map, sees a curve ahead, and slows down before you can even see it.
content.871c3a0e88d9: "Offline Road Knowledge." Downloads maps directly to your device storage so sunnypilot knows speed limits and sharp upcoming curves even when driving through remote areas with zero cell signal.
content.2ceceed03773: "Pro HUD Dash." Enhances your screen with rich telemetry: see the exact distance and speed of the car ahead, a color-coded G-force acceleration bar, and how long you have been stopped at a red light.

content.55deb657f8da: End-to-end (E2E) models are neural networks trained to map raw camera input directly to driving commands, rather than relying on hand-tuned perception → planning → control pipelines. The result is more human-like behavior in complex urban scenarios — stop signs, intersections, lane merges — at the cost of feeling slightly less rigid on straight highways. The WMI series and most 2025/2026 comma.ai releases are E2E.
